content.thinking:
I'm planning the kraken design: a rising sea creature with a domed mantle, glowing eyes, eight spreading tentacles with chains, suckers, and spikes, styled with bold bevelled Overwatch-like shapes and a single orange-cyan accent glow, scaled roughly six meters tall.

Now I'm figuring out the skeleton structure -- a root "body" joint, a spine chain for the mantle, a jaw with beak joints, and eight tentacle chains radiating from a ring around the body's base, each with five joints arcing outward and down to curl near the floor like they're emerging from water.

I'm varying each tentacle's reach, arch height, and curl direction with some randomness so a couple stand out dramatically, naming them t0 through t7 with joint suffixes, while keeping tip heights just barely above a thin water disc at the floor so nothing clips.

For the mantle, I'm sweeping a chain from the body upward through a few leaning-back points with a tapering radius curve down to a pointed tip, then planning a head region at the front for the eyes.

For the head, I'll add a separate scaled-sphere capsule, with glowing yellow-orange sclera eyes and dark slit pupils placed symmetrically. Palette-wise, I'm settling on deep purple-blue skin with a lighter belly tone and glowing orange accents, using custom countershading and stripe paints rather than a toon kit for a clean Overwatch-style blocking.

Writing custom paint and glow logic for bioluminescent mantle plates and tentacle suckers...

Adding darker inner sucker cylinders doubles the part count to around 250, plus I'm scattering a few dorsal spikes along each tentacle. For the mantle I'm considering lateral fins made from extruded outlines, though figuring out proper orthogonal axis directions for placement feels a bit tricky.

Now I'm working out the fin outline geometry, keeping it convex and non-self-intersecting with a thin bevel instead of risky smoothing. Then I move to the beak structure, setting up a jaw joint under the head aimed forward-and-down to hold the upper and lower beak cones.

Still adding teeth spikes to the jaw bone, then setting up the head as a scaled sphere attached to the body joint, and starting the mantle chain extending from behind the head.

Now I'm shaping the mantle path with a curved rise, assigning tapering radii along it, and checking that the overall kraken height (~5.4m) and tentacle reach (~5.7m radius) stay proportional. I'm also tracking the flat color budget before defining the mantle's skin paint.

For the paint logic, I'm blending a deep violet base dorsally with a cooler teal underside, using a mottled pattern plus a countershade toward a lighter belly tone. I'm layering in a dorsal ridge accent by checking the angular distance from the top (deg 0) and drawing a thin accent stripe there when near the ridge, falling back to the base coat elsewhere.

Then for the mantle, I'm composing nested stripe-and-mottle layers with a countershade toward the belly color, confirming paints can nest inside other paints. For the tentacles, I'm using a similar countershade-over-mottle approach shifted toward a tentacle-specific belly tone, considering whether to add a tip accent via sweeping bands or just a direct paint assignment.

I'm now working through sucker placement along the tentacle underside, deciding on angle offsets for a staggered double row and estimating counts per tentacle to get a rough total sucker count across the creature.

I'm also working out the sucker geometry itself—a simple cylinder-and-disc shape for rim and inner color—plus naming the joint chains for each tentacle so they're properly tagged for the skeleton, and starting to lay out the catmull-rom path points for the tentacle curve from the body base.

Now I'm sweeping each tentacle chain with a tapering radius profile (starting thick near the head socket and narrowing to a rounded tip), making sure the root points sit correctly inside the head sphere's geometry, and figuring out the angular spacing to place each tentacle evenly around the body facing forward.

Working out curl and arch for the tentacle tips...

Finalizing the raised tentacle curve points, capping height near the mantle, then adding a water disc rigidly attached to the body for the floor base.

I'm now layering foam details: flat torus rings around the tentacle tips and body base, plus a radial-gradient water paint function that generates teal rings via a modulo pattern on distance from center.

For texture I'm scattering about 14 random splash droplet spheres around the creature, then positioning the eyes on the head's front surface using the ellipsoid equation to find the correct z-depth, placing glowing orange sclera spheres slightly embedded at that point.

Still shaping eye details...

I'm thinking about adding head accents next, maybe a crest of spikes running from the head to the mantle, each defined by a base point, direction, length, and radius for a bony, textured look.

Adding small oral tentacles near the mouth, with curling forward-down paths for four short feeding arms.

I'm shaping the beak with an upper and lower spike for the mouth, dark horn-colored, and setting up a flat color palette for the creature.

Now I'm setting up imports for the mesh builder, paint utilities, and glow effects, planning to use countershade, mottle, and stripe helpers to texture the body realistically.

Adding tentacle spikes and water droplets...

Now I'm sizing up the sucker geometry—stacking a rim cylinder and a slightly smaller inner cylinder on the same frame so the inner disc sits proud of the rim by a hair.

Then I'm tallying tentacle part counts: eight tentacles each with sweep segments, two rows of nine suckers, and spikes, totaling roughly 330 parts, which seems manageable.

Now I'm adding a tiny white highlight sphere on the eye for shine, scaling the pupil geometry, then building mirrored fins on both sides attached to the mantle's second joint with extrusion, bevel, and a painted ridge pattern.

For the head paint, I'm countershading the mottled base toward the belly tone with slight brow striping. Then I'll finalize all the part counts and handle the mantle sweep ridge color, measuring the dorsal angle as the minimum between itself and its complement around 360.
